easy.def: Just right, with nothing wrong.
examples: What is the exact time?
This is the exact spot.
Give me the exact number.

more.def: Completely correct, with no mistakes.
examples: The exact time is four fifteen.
She counted out the exact change for the bus.
Scientists need exact measurements for the experiment.

easy.def: Just right, with no mistake.
examples: It fits exactly.
That is exactly right.
She knew exactly what to do.

more.def: In a way that is completely correct, with nothing more or less.
examples: The two pieces fit together exactly.
It is exactly three o'clock.
I knew exactly where I had put my keys.

easy.def: To make something sound bigger than it is.
examples: Do not exaggerate.
He exaggerated the fish's size.
She exaggerated her story.

more.def: To say that something is bigger, better or worse than it really is.
examples: He exaggerated how big the fish was.
Do not exaggerate when you tell the story.
She exaggerated the size of the spider.

easy.def: A test.
examples: I have an exam.
The exam is on math.
I passed the exam.

more.def: A test that shows how much you know.
examples: I studied for my math exam.
The exam had twenty questions.
She was glad to pass the exam.

easy.def: A test.
examples: We had an examination.
The examination was long.
I passed the examination.

more.def: A test of what you know, or a careful look at something.
examples: We had a spelling examination.
The doctor gave me a careful examination.
The examination had twenty questions.

easy.def: To look at something very closely.
examples: The doctor will examine my ear.
I examine the bug with my eyes.
The vet examines our dog.

more.def: To look at or check something carefully to learn more about it.
examples: We examined the leaf under a magnifying glass.
The detective examined the room for clues.
She examined the coin closely to read its date.

related.def: A person who looks closely at something to check it.

easy.def: One thing that shows what others are like.
examples: Give me an example.
A dog is an example of a pet.
This is a good example.

more.def: One thing that shows what a group of things is like.
examples: A cat is an example of a pet.
Can you give an example of a mammal?
The teacher showed an example of a good story.

easy.def: Very, very good.
examples: You did an excellent job.
The food was excellent.
She is an excellent swimmer.

more.def: Extremely good; better than most.
examples: You did an excellent job on your project.
The restaurant has excellent soup.
He is an excellent chess player.

easy.def: But not.
examples: Everyone came except Sam.
I like all fruit except pears.
The store is open every day except Sunday.

more.def: Not including; leaving out.
examples: Everyone in the class went on the trip except Jo, who was sick.
All of the animals, except the lions, were awake.
The library is open every day except Sunday.

easy.def: Something that is not the same as the others.
examples: Every cat likes milk, with one exception.
There is an exception to the rule.
She is the exception.

more.def: A person or thing that does not follow the rule.
examples: Everyone came on time, with one exception.
There is an exception to every rule.
My cat is the exception, since she loves water.

easy.def: To give one thing and get another.
examples: We exchange cards.
I will exchange this shirt for a bigger one.
They exchanged gifts.

more.def: To give something and get something else in return.
examples: The kids exchanged stickers at lunch.
Dad exchanged the shirt for a larger size.
The two teams exchanged gifts after the game.

easy.def: Trading one thing for another.
examples: A swap is an exchange.
The exchange of cards was fun.
We made an exchange.

more.def: The act of giving one thing and getting another in its place.
examples: The class held a book exchange in the library.
We made an exchange: my apple for his cookie.
An exchange of letters kept the two friends close.

easy.def: Very happy and full of energy.
examples: I am excited for my birthday.
The kids were excited.
She felt excited.

more.def: Feeling very happy and eager about something.
examples: We were excited about the trip to the zoo.
The excited puppy wagged its tail.
She was excited to start school.

easy.def: In an excited way.
examples: The kids talked excitedly.
She jumped excitedly.
He opened the gift excitedly.

more.def: In a way that shows you are thrilled.
examples: The kids talked excitedly about the trip.
She jumped up and down excitedly.
The puppy barked excitedly.

easy.def: A feeling of being thrilled.
examples: The kids jumped with excitement.
I felt excitement.
The excitement was high.

more.def: A strong, happy feeling that makes you eager about something.
examples: The children jumped up and down with excitement.
There was a lot of excitement before the trip.
I could hardly sleep because of the excitement.

easy.def: Making you feel very happy and eager.
examples: The game was exciting.
An exciting day.
What an exciting story!

more.def: Causing strong feelings of interest or joy.
examples: The last minute of the game was exciting.
We went on an exciting trip.
She read an exciting story about a pirate.

easy.def: Only for a few people.
examples: The club is exclusive.
It is an exclusive party.
An exclusive pool.

more.def: Not shared with others, or open only to a few people.
examples: The club is exclusive and only lets in a few members.
It was an exclusive party for her close friends.
The pool is exclusive to hotel guests.

easy.def: To say it is okay that someone did something.
examples: Please excuse me.
He excused her.
Excuse my mess.

more.def: To forgive a small mistake, or to let someone leave.
examples: Please excuse me for being late to class.
The teacher excused the students for lunch.
She excused his mistake because it was an accident.

easy.def: A reason you give for something you did.
examples: I have an excuse.
His excuse was silly.
That is not a good excuse.

more.def: A reason that you give to explain why something happened or was not done.
examples: His excuse for being late was that the bus broke down.
She had no excuse for forgetting her homework.
Rain is not an excuse to stay inside all day.

easy.def: To carry out a plan or order.
examples: The team executed the plan.
She executed a perfect jump.
He executed the order.

more.def: To do or carry out something, such as a plan or a movement.
examples: The team executed the plan perfectly.
The gymnast executed a perfect jump.
The workers executed the orders they were given.

easy.def: Moving your body to stay strong and healthy.
examples: I get exercise at recess.
Walking is good exercise.
Dogs need exercise.

more.def: Activity that makes your body stronger, such as running or swimming.
examples: Running around the playground is good exercise.
The doctor said exercise helps our hearts stay healthy.
The dog gets exercise on long walks.

easy.def: A task you do to practice something.
examples: The math exercise was easy.
We did a spelling exercise.
Do the first exercise.

more.def: A set of questions or tasks that you do to practice a skill.
examples: The teacher gave us a reading exercise.
Each exercise on the page has five questions.
We did a math exercise on fractions.

easy.def: To move your body to stay strong.
examples: I exercise every day.
We exercised in the gym.
They exercise their dogs.

more.def: To do activities that make your body strong and healthy.
examples: She exercises by riding her bike.
We exercised in gym class by running laps.
Cats and dogs both need to exercise.

easy.def: Very, very tired.
examples: I was exhausted after the long walk.
The exhausted baby fell asleep.
We were exhausted after the swim.

more.def: Extremely tired, with no energy left.
examples: After the race, the exhausted runners lay down on the grass.
The exhausted hikers finally reached their camp.
I was exhausted from staying up too late.

easy.def: A show of things in a museum.
examples: We saw a dinosaur exhibit.
The exhibit is new.
The exhibit has old coins.

more.def: A group of objects shown to the public, as in a museum.
examples: We saw a dinosaur exhibit at the museum.
The art exhibit has paintings by children.
The exhibit about space was my favorite.

easy.def: To show something to the public.
examples: The museum exhibits old coins.
She exhibited her paintings.
The class exhibited their art.

more.def: To put something on display for people to see.
examples: The museum exhibits ancient pots.
She exhibited her paintings at the fair.
The class exhibited its science projects.

easy.def: To be real.
examples: Dinosaurs existed long ago.
Dragons do not exist.
Unicorns do not exist.

more.def: To be real, or to be alive.
examples: Dinosaurs existed millions of years ago.
Dragons do not exist outside of stories.
Life exists on Earth.

easy.def: Being real.
examples: The existence of dinosaurs is proven.
The scientist doubted its existence.
The existence of the lake is known.

more.def: The state of being alive or real.
examples: The existence of dinosaurs is proven by fossils.
Scientists studied the existence of life on other planets.
The lake came into existence long ago.

easy.def: A way out of a place.
examples: The exit is on the left.
We left through the exit.
The sign points to the exit.

more.def: A door or passage that you use to leave a place.
examples: Follow the green sign to the exit.
The theater has an exit on each side.
We took the next exit off the highway.

easy.def: To go out of a place.
examples: Please exit the bus.
We exited the building.
She exited through the back door.

more.def: To leave a place.
examples: Please exit the bus through the back door.
The actors exited the stage.
We exited the highway to find lunch.

easy.def: From a faraway place and unusual.
examples: An exotic bird.
Exotic fruit.
The exotic plant is rare.

more.def: Strange and exciting because it comes from a faraway place.
examples: The zoo has an exotic bird from the rainforest.
We tasted an exotic fruit.
The shop sold exotic spices.

easy.def: To get bigger.
examples: The balloon expands.
The town expanded.
Metal expands in heat.

more.def: To grow bigger in size or amount, or to make something bigger.
examples: The balloon expanded as I blew into it.
The town expanded when new houses were built.
Metal expands when it is heated.

easy.def: To think something will happen.
examples: I expect it will rain.
We expect Grandma at noon.
She expected a gift.

more.def: To believe that something will happen or that someone will arrive.
examples: We expect the first snow to fall sometime next week.
The teacher expects everyone to bring a pencil.
I was expecting a letter, but nothing came today.

easy.def: What you think will happen.
examples: I have high expectations.
His expectation was to win.
The result met her expectations.

more.def: A belief that something will happen or that someone will do something.
examples: I have high expectations for the show.
Her expectation was that the bus would be on time.
The trip did not meet our expectations.

easy.def: A long trip for a special reason.
examples: The explorers went on an expedition.
The expedition was long.
They planned an expedition.

more.def: A long, organized trip to explore or study a place.
examples: The explorers went on an expedition to the Arctic.
The scientists planned an expedition to the jungle.
The expedition took three months.

easy.def: To force out.
examples: The student was expelled.
The fan expels air.
The volcano expels ash.

more.def: To force something out, or to make someone leave a school.
examples: The fan expels the hot air from the room.
The volcano expelled ash into the sky.
The club expelled the member for breaking the rules.

easy.def: Money you spend.
examples: The trip was an expense.
The expense was high.
We counted the expense.

more.def: Money that you spend on something, or the cost of something.
examples: The trip was a big expense for the family.
Dad wrote down every expense.
A new roof is a large expense.

easy.def: Costing a lot of money.
examples: The big toy is expensive.
That coat is too expensive.
Gold is expensive.

more.def: Costing more money than most people want to spend.
examples: The new computer was too expensive for us to buy.
Diamonds are expensive because they are rare.
An expensive meal at a fancy place can cost a lot.

easy.def: Something that happens to you.
examples: The trip was a fun experience.
Camping was a new experience.
It was a scary experience.

more.def: Something you do or that happens to you.
examples: Riding a horse was a new experience for me.
The trip to the cave was an exciting experience.
She shared the experience with her friends.

easy.def: What you know from doing something.
examples: She has experience with horses.
A guide with experience led us.
Experience helps you do better.

more.def: Knowledge or skill that you get from doing something for a long time.
examples: The guide had years of experience climbing mountains.
Experience taught him to check the weather before hiking.
You need experience to fly a plane.

easy.def: A test to find out something.
examples: We did an experiment with ice and salt.
In our experiment, the egg floated.
The experiment made bubbles.

more.def: A careful test done to discover or prove something.
examples: Our science experiment showed that plants grow toward light.
The scientist repeated the experiment to check her results.
As an experiment, we tried baking the bread without sugar.

easy.def: A person who knows a lot about something.
examples: He is a bird expert.
The expert fixed it.
She is a math expert.

more.def: A person who has special skill or knows a lot about a subject.
examples: The bird expert identified the song.
An expert fixed the broken clock.
She is an expert at chess.

easy.def: To tell how or why.
examples: Please explain the game.
She explained the rules.
He explains how it works.

more.def: To make something clear by giving details or reasons.
examples: The teacher explained how plants make food from sunlight.
Can you explain why the sky is blue?
She explained the rules of the game to the new player.

easy.def: Words that tell why or how something happens.
examples: The teacher gave an explanation.
I asked for an explanation.
Her explanation was clear.

more.def: A statement that tells how something works or why something happened.
examples: The teacher gave a clear explanation of how plants grow.
He had a good explanation for being late.
The book's explanation of the water cycle had a diagram.

easy.def: To burst with a loud bang.
examples: The balloon will explode.
The firework exploded.
The popcorn exploded in the pan.

more.def: To burst apart suddenly and loudly.
examples: The balloon exploded with a loud pop.
The firework exploded in the sky.
The volcano exploded and sent ash into the air.

easy.def: To look around a new place.
examples: Let's explore the garden!
We explore the beach for shells.
The cat explores the new house.

more.def: To travel through or look carefully at a place to learn about it.
examples: The divers explored a cave deep under the sea.
Robots explore the surface of Mars.
On vacation, we explored the old part of the city.

easy.def: A sudden, loud burst.
examples: We heard an explosion.
The firework made an explosion.
The explosion was loud.

more.def: A sudden, very loud burst that sends things flying.
examples: A loud explosion came from the old factory.
Fireworks make bright explosions in the sky.
A volcano can cause a huge explosion.

easy.def: Able to blow up.
examples: Fireworks are explosive.
Gas can be explosive.
The explosive material was kept far away.

more.def: Likely to burst or blow up with a loud bang.
examples: Fireworks are explosive, so only adults should light them.
The volcano had an explosive eruption.
Gas can be explosive near a flame.

easy.def: To let something be seen or touched.
examples: Do not expose the film to light.
The wind exposed the rocks.
The low tide exposes the sand.

more.def: To uncover something so it can be seen, or to leave something open to weather or danger.
examples: The low tide exposed the rocks along the shore.
Do not expose the paint to too much sun.
The fox's cover was exposed when the snow melted.

easy.def: Being left open to something.
examples: Too much exposure to sun burns skin.
Exposure to cold can make you sick.
The exposure was brief.

more.def: The state of being open to something, such as the sun or cold.
examples: Too much exposure to the sun can burn your skin.
Exposure to cold air made her shiver.
The exposure to loud noise hurt his ears.

easy.def: To show how you feel or what you think.
examples: I express my feelings.
She expressed her thanks.
He expressed his idea in words.

more.def: To let others know what you think or feel, in words, art or actions.
examples: She expressed her thanks with a card.
Painting helps him express his feelings.
The children expressed their ideas in drawings.

easy.def: The look on someone's face.
examples: She had a happy expression.
His expression was sad.
I saw a surprised expression.

more.def: A look on a person's face that shows what they feel.
examples: She had a happy expression on her face.
His expression changed when he heard the news.
The baby's funny expression made us laugh.

easy.def: A group of words with a special meaning.
examples: "Piece of cake" is an expression.
He used a funny expression.
That is a common expression.

more.def: A word or group of words that people use to say something.
examples: "Piece of cake" is an expression that means easy.
She used a funny expression I had never heard.
"It's raining cats and dogs" is a well-known expression.

easy.def: To make longer or reach out.
examples: I extend my hand.
The road extends to the sea.
We extended the visit.

more.def: To stretch out, make longer, or go farther.
examples: The road extends all the way to the sea.
She extended her hand to say hello.
We extended our vacation by two days.

easy.def: An extra part that makes something longer.
examples: The house has an extension.
I plugged in an extension cord.
We got an extension on the homework.

more.def: An extra part added to make something longer, or more time added.
examples: The house has a new extension at the back.
I used an extension cord for the lamp.
The teacher gave us an extension on the project.

easy.def: No longer living anywhere on Earth.
examples: Dinosaurs are extinct.
Some animals may go extinct.
The extinct bird had a big beak.

more.def: No longer existing; having no living members left.
examples: The dodo bird became extinct hundreds of years ago.
Woolly mammoths have been extinct for thousands of years.
People are working to keep tigers from becoming extinct.

easy.def: More than usual.
examples: I need an extra pencil.
We have extra time.
Take an extra cookie.

more.def: More than what is usual or needed.
examples: Bring an extra sweater in case it gets cold.
We had extra time before the bus came.
Add an extra spoon of sugar.

easy.def: Very special and not usual.
examples: The view was extraordinary.
She has an extraordinary gift.
It was an extraordinary day.

more.def: Far beyond what is usual, amazing.
examples: The view from the mountain was extraordinary.
She has an extraordinary talent for music.
It was an extraordinary day I will never forget.

easy.def: Very great.
examples: It was extreme heat.
The cold is extreme.
He took extreme care.

more.def: Much greater than usual, or at the very end of a range.
examples: The extreme heat made us stay inside.
The climbers took extreme care on the icy rocks.
She is an extreme sports fan.
